newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Two killed in Karachi violence, shops closed.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in Karachi violence, shops closed.

text.p: At least two people were killed on Thursday in Pakistan's volatile city of Karachi, where shops were forced to remain closed for the third day after an attack on an ethnic party's office, police said.

They said an unidentified young man was kidnapped and strangled. His body, wrapped in a bag, was found at Mominabad in the city's District West. Bashir Sukhi, 50, was shot dead in his home at Korangi in District East.
The deaths raised the toll to more than 100 in ethnic, sectarian and political violence in Karachi so far this year compared to 500 in 1996 and 2,000 in 1995.
Violence has surged in this industrial port city in recent weeks on renewed tension between the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and its breakaway Haqiqi faction.
Witnesses said most shopping centres were shut for the third day in a strike enforced by MQM militants after nine people, including five MQM workers, were killed by gunmen on Monday.
The MQM's London-based leader Altaf Hussain ordered the closure of more than 100 party offices in Karachi after Monday's deadly attack on an MQM branch.

The MQM, long involved in a struggle with security forces as well as with Haqiqi, was brought into a coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, after national and provincial elections in February.
On Wednesday, 11 people were killed in separate incidents of violence.
